title: diagrammer stage-1 code graph
description: What an AST parser proved about a source tree. Structure and raw references only: no meaning is attributed here, because stage 2 is where meaning is added. This document is the input a plugin's skill reads.

schema_version.description: Bumped when a change would make an older reader misread a newer document. A reader that does not recognise the value refuses the document rather than consuming part of it.

generated_by.description: Free text naming the producer and its version, for provenance. Carries no contractual meaning and is not read by any stage.

root.description: Id of the single node with no parent. Every other node reaches it by following parent pointers.

nodes.description: Sorted by id. The order is part of the byte-identity guarantee, not a convenience.

edges.description: Sorted by (from, to, kind). References at the finest resolution the analyzer could prove; rolling them up to a coarser level is a later stage's job.

nodeId.description: Unique within the document. Conventionally a kind prefix and a path, such as pkg:net/http or fn:net/http.(*Server).Serve. Any printable text without spaces or control characters is accepted, because ids are derived from source paths rather than authored. Uniqueness is checked by validate, since a pattern cannot express it.

nodeKind.description: group is a directory holding only other directories; package is a directory holding source; file, type and func are what they say. Every analyzer projects its language onto these five, whatever that language calls them.

name.description: For display. Not an identifier: two nodes may share a name.

parent.description: Absent on the root node and present on every other. validate rejects a parent that names no node, and rejects a cycle.

sourceRef.description: Where the node was found. The path is relative to the analyzed root, so a graph does not leak the machine that produced it.

edgeKind.description: import is a declared dependency between packages or files; call is one function reaching another. Ordered coarsest to finest evidence.

weight.description: How many times the reference was observed. One edge per (from, to, kind); repeated references raise the weight rather than adding a row.

diagnostics.description: What the analyzer could not do. This block exists because tree-sitter fails soft: it emits an ERROR node and carries on, so code can vanish from a graph that otherwise looks complete. A failure that is not recorded here is indistinguishable from source that was never there.

files_parsed.description: Files the analyzer read, whether or not they parsed. Compare against the length of parse_failures to get the success count; the count is not stored twice.

parse_failures.description: One entry per file that failed, sorted by path. An empty array asserts that every file parsed, which is a claim the fixtures test.

unresolved_references.description: References seen but not resolved to a node, grouped by reason. Reported rather than gated: resolution rates differ by language and a low rate is a known property of the parser, not a defect in the document.
